question.leadin: This period of less than ten years caused its country's population to drop by nearly twenty percent.
question.text: Name this period of disease and starvation caused by infected plants that affected a constituent country of the United Kingdom from 1845 to 1852.
question.answerHtml: Irish Potato Famine (or Great Famine ; or Great Hunger ; accept Gorta Mor )
question.clue: Protestant missionaries set up schools during this event in an act called "souperism."

swap.leadin: Eamon de Valera founded this nation's largest political party, Fianna Fail.
swap.text: Name this nation, with capital at Dublin. Its northern neighbor is still part of the United Kingdom.
swap.clue: Leaders from this country include Eamon de Valera and Patrick Pearse.

question.text: Gladstone unsuccessfully pushed for the home rule of this country first conquered by Henry VIII. The failed Easter Rising occurred in this nation, which was also home to the Battle of the Boyne.
question.clue: Eamon de Valera became the first Taoiseach of this country after forming the Fianna Fail party.

swap.text: During the crisis of the Third Century Aurelian built a set of these structures around Rome. Antonius Pius and Hadrian each built one of these structures that marked the northern border of the empire.
swap.answerHtml: walls [accept Aurelian Walls; accept Severan Walls; accept Hadrian’s Wall; accept Antonine Wall]
swap.clue: Construction of Austrian towns characterized by this feature rapidly increased in the 11th century.

question.text: de Valera and his supporters broke from this Irish party in 1926, whose name translates to "We Ourselves." This party has since gotten involved in Northern Irish politics, and is associated with the Irish Republican Army.
question.clue: Former Tanaiste Eamon Gilmore was originally a member of this party before eventually joining the Labour Party.

swap.text: The Dail Eireann sits in this city, the capital of Ireland.
swap.clue: The disguised ship Aud failed to supply arms to this city for an uprising that Roger Casement tried to join.

question.leadin: The Fianna ("fi-na") was a major supporter of this rebellion.
question.text: Name this 1916 anti-British rebellion organized by the IRB which began on a namesake holiday and was centered at the General Post Office. It was defeated by 16,000 British soldiers after a week.
question.answerHtml: Easter Rising [or Easter Rebellion; accept Éiri Amach na Cásca; prompt on partial]
question.clue: Tom Clarke planned this event, and, like Joseph Plunkett and John MacBride, he was executed for taking part.

swap.text: This agreement, negotiated in 1998 with the help of Tony Blair, ended the Troubles by effectively dismantling the Provisional IRA.
swap.clue: Bertie Ahern and David Andrews were signatories of this document, which was primarily negotiated by David Trimble and John Hume.

question.text: This leader of the Land League gave the speech that incited the original boycott. As an MP, he convinced members of the Liberal Party to support Irish Home Rule.
question.clue: His demise came after the Nonconformist movement of his political party, after seeing a letter written to John Rowley, voted him out of a position of leadership after he was married to Kitty O'Shea.

swap.leadin: [Moderator: Do not read "Irish" or "Ireland" in the answer if the first part is missed] It was the political goal of Isaac Butt, and the legislation providing for it failed twice, in 1886 and 1893.
swap.text: John Redmond nearly achieved what political ambition, supported by Charles Parnell and opposed by the Orange Order?
swap.answerHtml: Irish Home Rule [or the Government of Ireland Act; or the independence of Ireland]
swap.clue: Edward Carson and James Craig, leaders of the Unionists, campaigned against a 1914 bill aiming to bring about this outcome.

question.leadin: Answer the following about poor British governmental responses to hunger strikes.
question.text: Margaret Thatcher pronounced this IRA member to be a "criminal" who "chose to take his own life" after he died following a 66-day hunger strike in Maze Prison.
question.clue: Winston Churchill Boulevard in Tehran was renamed for this man, prompting the British Embassy to move their main address onto a side street.

swap.text: In response to the Irish Republican Army's assassination of former Viceroy of India Louis Mountbatten, this politician asserted Mountbatten "knew the danger" involved in coming to Ireland could possibly lead to his "execution." This man served as the leader of Sinn Fein ("shin fayn") from 1983 until 2018.
swap.clue: In interviews for an oral history project conducted by Boston College, Brendan Hughes and Dolours Price implicated this person in the murder of Jean McConville.

question.text: The Armagh disturbances were part of a conflict in this historic province, much of which now makes up Northern Ireland. The Scots-Irish principally lived in this northernmost province.
question.clue: This province was the site of an early 17th century "plantation," in which James I settled thousands of Scots here.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about some of the more violent aspects of Irish history.
swap.text: The 1882 assassinations of British chief secretary of Ireland, Lord Cavendish, and his under-secretary Thomas Henry Burke, are named after the where they were committed. The killings were apparently perpetrated by members of an Irish secret society known as "The Invincibles."
swap.clue: It resulted in the death of a man married to Prime Minister Gladstone's niece.

question.text: Before founding the British Union of Fascists, Oswald Mosley left the Conservative Party for the Labour Party over the use of this anti-IRA unit of the British Army. They took their name from the colors of their mixed uniforms.
question.answerHtml: Black and Tans [or Royal Irish Constabulary Special Reserve]
question.clue: Members of this group were paid just 10 shillings per day, and most were veterans of World War I. This group killed 12 people in Croke Park at a football match in the aftermath of Bloody Sunday.

swap.text: The vicar proved his loyalty to James II by "shout[ing] down" laws of this type, exemplified by the Clarendon Code and the Test Acts that prohibited Catholics from holding office. A similar set of laws were enacted in Ireland.
swap.answerHtml: Penal Laws [anti-prompt on Clarendon Code or Test Acts before they are mentioned]
swap.clue: One major goal of the United Irishmen was the repeal of these discriminatory laws, which prevented Irish Catholics from holding public office and severely restricted their right to inherit land.

question.text: This younger sister of Charles Parnell led the Ladies' Land League and wrote The Tale of a Great Sham. A plaque on her tombstone carries her quote "the best part of independence; the independence of mind."
question.answerHtml: Anna Catherine Parnell [grudgingly prompt on (A.) Parnell ]

swap.text: 's single most violent incident of the troubles was the August 1998 car bombing in this city, attributed to a faction calling itself the Real IRA.

question.text: Letters printed in The Times that purported to demonstrate Parnell's support for the Phoenix Park murders were eventually revealed to be forgeries created by this journalist.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the death of T.H. Burke FTPE.
swap.text: On May 6, 1882 surgical knives were used to off Burke and his boss Lord Frederick Cavendish at this site that now gives the grisly event its name.
swap.clue: Parnell was initially accused of involvement in the May 1882 murders of Lord Cavendish and his undersecretary in this Dublin location. The murders had been carried out by the nationalist terrorist group The Invincibles.
